correctness.rationale: The exact line-search formula gives successor-gradient orthogonality. The Euclidean ratio is reduced to two spectral moments and bounded sharply by the endpoint secant inequality, with maximum (kappa-1)^2/(4 kappa). Projecting a coordinate vector onto the orthogonal complement of the current gradient then gives the sharp geometric factor sqrt(n-1). The explicit two-plane SPD construction has eigenvalues 1 and kappa and simultaneously attains both equalities. Solving the resulting scalar inequality gives the stated dimension-dependent frontier.

value.rationale: The maximum absolute gradient component is a natural coordinatewise stationarity diagnostic. The theorem gives a complete sharp dimension-and-conditioning law, not a generic norm-equivalence estimate: exact-line-search orthogonality improves sqrt(n) to the attained sqrt(n-1), and the safety threshold collapses toward one as dimension grows. The explicit witness shows that this diagnostic can worsen even when the Euclidean gradient norm and objective improve, making the distinction operationally meaningful rather than merely a change of norm.
